speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, along with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee today, and episodes of pain when you urinate. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the affected joints?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome). The triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle, now knee) and urethritis, combined with a history of unprotected sexual activity, is highly characteristic; further testing (urinalysis, RF, HLA-B27) is unnecessary to confirm this clinical diagnosis.
